title: Di San Xian (Stir-Fried Potato, Aubergine and Green Pepper)
summary: Aubergine soaked and coated in cornflour, fried with potato wedges and green pepper, then tossed in a glossy sauce of soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar with garlic and spring onion.
equipment: large bowl and a plate to weigh it down
wok or deep frying pan (35 cm)
baking tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for soaking
green pepper, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.note: 2 tsp for the sauce, 2 tsp for the aubergine

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately

steps.title: Soak the aubergine
steps.text: Stir the soaking salt into the cold water in the large bowl, add the aubergine and weigh it down with a plate for 15 min. Soaking stops the aubergine from drinking up too much oil. Meanwhile, whisk the 60 ml water, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and 2 tsp cornflour in the small bowl.

steps.title: Fry the vegetables
steps.text: Drain the aubergine, pat it dry and toss with the remaining 2 tsp cornflour. Heat the frying oil in the wok to 190 °C. Fry the aubergine in two batches for about 3 min until tender and golden, keeping the oil at 175-190 °C, and drain on the paper. Fry the potatoes in two batches for 5-7 min until golden and tender to a knife, then fry the pepper for 30-60 seconds until blistered. Drain.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Carefully pour the oil out of the wok (keep it for another use) and wipe it clean. Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium heat and stir-fry the spring onion whites and garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Stir the sauce, pour it in and simmer for about 1 min until thick and glossy. Add all the vegetables and toss for about 1 min until coated and hot. Scatter with the spring onion greens and serve with rice.

tips: Roll-cutting (turning the vegetable a quarter turn between cuts) gives more surface for browning and sauce.
Never leave hot oil unattended, and lower the vegetables in gently with a slotted spoon.
Cool the used oil, strain it and keep it for your next fry.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten at once. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a hot wok until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
